<!--
  Build pipeline for this manuscript (first draft, 2026-11-06)
  ============================================================

  This Rmd runs no simulation code. helpers.R (this folder) loads the
  stored summaries below and defines the formatting helpers. Paths are
  relative to the repository root. Origin of the prose: paper 02's
  report.Rmd at commit c866404be (sections sec-comparators,
  sec-pathways, sec-alternatives, sec-prognostic, sec-trend,
  sec-random, "What the expectancy terms are for", and the matching
  Limitations, Conclusions and Glossary items), rewritten against the
  published-set reruns of docs/74.

  Published-set runs (Hendrickson et al.'s parameter values, stop on
  non-positive-definite matrices; docs/74, wave 1, 2026-11-03/04):
    28-run-g9-prognostic-stress.R --params published
      -> analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/published/g9-prognostic-stress/

      -> .../published/g9-gap-fill/C/

      -> .../published/referee-variants/block-{T,N,A}/

      -> .../published/tier1-g-vs-f-e0/

      -> .../published/g-vs-f-comparison/

  Historical exhibit (simcore2026 parameter set, silent repair; kept
  under docs/74 decision D5, not rerun):
    28-run-g9-prognostic-stress.R (job 28, 2026-10-25)
      -> analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/g9-prognostic-stress/summary.rds
    29-run-g9-random-effects.R (job 30, 2026-10-26)
      -> analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/g9-random-effects/summary.rds
    30-check-prognostic-confound-pd.R (analytic, simcore2026 SDs)
      -> .../g9-prognostic-stress/pd-check.rds
    31-prognostic-coupling-ceiling.R (analytic, correlation matrix only)
      -> .../g9-prognostic-stress/coupling-ceilings.rds
    34-referee-reanalysis.R
      -> .../referee-reanalysis/m12-random-effects.csv

  Not yet run: the biomarker-by-time block of split plan Section 3.1.
  Its section is a marked placeholder with no numbers.

  Render through tools/render.sh, never rmarkdown::render() directly.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
## The repository root is the first parent holding DESCRIPTION. The
## here package is not assumed, since the host R session may lack it.

  d <- normalizePath(getwd())
  while (!file.exists(file.path(d, 'DESCRIPTION')) &&
           d != dirname(d)) d <- dirname(d)
```

```{r values-provenance, include = FALSE}
                  scen = s21_m)

  setv('sig_br', sprintf('%g', sigma_br))
  setv('sig_pb', sprintf('%g', sigma_pb))
  setv('truth45', fs2(-0.45 * sigma_br))
  setv('truth30', fs2(-0.30 * sigma_br))
}

  setv('sig_pb_sc', sprintf('%g', sigma_pb_simcore))
```

```{r values-ceil, include = FALSE}
if (has_ceil) {
  cr <- ceil$results
  bnd <- function(cp, g) cr$ceiling[cr$coupling == cp & cr$given == g]
  setv('b_bm', f3(bnd('c_bm', 'alone')))
  setv('b_pb', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'alone')))
  setv('b_pb30', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.3')))
  setv('b_pb45', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45')))
  setv('b_bl30', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3')))
  setv('b_bl45', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.45')))
  claim(is.na(bnd('c_bm', 'c_pb = 0.6')) &&
          is.na(bnd('c_bm', 'c_tv = 0.6')),
        'No c_bm is feasible with c_pb or c_tv at 0.6.')
  claim(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45') > 0.3,
        'Strength 0.3 lies inside the bound at c_bm = 0.45.')
}
```

```{r values-stress, include = FALSE}
if (has_st_p) {
  n_st <- st_p_m$n_reps
  setv('st_n', fn(n_st))
  setv('st_band', band_txt(n_st))
  s3n <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0, pathway != 'progtvgrow')
  g9n <- s3n |> filter(method == 'E7cr2')
  g10n <- s3n |> filter(method == 'E7null_cr2')
  fbn <- s3n |> filter(method == 'F1A0B')
  setv('st_g9_null', rng(g9n$reject))
  setv('st_g10_null', rng(g10n$reject))
  setv('st_fb_null', rng(fbn$reject))
  claim(all(in_band(g9n$reject, n_st)),
        'Stress job: G9 null inside the band at strength 0.3.')
  claim(all(in_band(g10n$reject, n_st)),
        'Stress job: G10 null inside the band at strength 0.3.')
  pw <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0.45,
           method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1A0B')) |>
    select(pathway, N, method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = reject)
  setv('st_g9_alt', rng(pw$E7cr2))
  setv('st_fb_g10', rng(pw$F1A0B - pw$E7null_cr2, fs3))
  tvg <- st_p |>
    filter(pathway == 'progtvgrow') |>
    select(c_bm, N, method, strength, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = strength, values_from = reject,
                names_prefix = 's')
  claim(isTRUE(all.equal(tvg$s0.3, tvg$s0.6)),
        'Constant shift: identical rejection at both strengths.')
  cells <- st_p |>
    group_by(cell_id, pathway, strength, c_bm, N) |>
    summarise(nmax = max(n, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  six <- cells |> filter(strength == 0.6, pathway != 'progtvgrow')
  setv('n6_cells', nrow(six))
  setv('n6_refused', sum(six$nmax == 0))
  refused <- six |> filter(nmax == 0)
  setv('n6_ran', sum(six$nmax > 0))
  if (has_pdc) {
    rep_cfg <- pdc$summary |>
      filter(paths_repaired > 0) |>
      transmute(key = paste(pathway, strength, c_bm))
    ref_cfg <- unique(paste(refused$pathway, refused$strength,
                            refused$c_bm))
    claim(setequal(rep_cfg$key, ref_cfg),
          paste('The published rerun refused exactly the',
                'configurations that the historical check repaired.'))
  }
  if (has_rvA) {
    ref <- rvA |>
      filter(method == 'E7cr2', t1half == 0.5, c_bm == 0.45) |>
      select(N, ref = reject)
    s3a <- st_p |>
      filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0.45, method == 'E7cr2',
             pathway != 'progtvgrow') |>
      left_join(ref, by = 'N')
    setv('a_n', fn(rvA_m$reps_alt))
    setv('ref35', f3(ref$ref[ref$N == 35]))
    setv('ref70', f3(ref$ref[ref$N == 70]))
    dlt <- s3a$reject - s3a$ref
    imx <- which.max(abs(dlt))
    setv('st_g9_dmax', fs3(dlt[imx]))
    claim(s3a$pathway[imx] == 'progpb' && dlt[imx] > 0,
          paste('Stress job: the largest G9 power difference from the',
                'reference is a gain under the placebo-response path.'))
  }
}
if (has_s21) {
  a <- s21 |> filter(cell == 'hybrid_null') |> arrange(method)
  b <- s21 |> filter(cell == 'progtvgrow_null') |> arrange(method)
  dd <- max(abs(a$reject - b$reject), na.rm = TRUE)
  setv('abs_dd', f4(dd))
  claim(dd == 0, 'Constant shift reproduces the null cell exactly.')
}
```

```{r values-blockN, include = FALSE}
if (has_rvN) {
  nN <- rvN |> filter(c_pb > 0)
  ids <- unique(nN$cell_id)
  pN <- rvNp |> filter(cell_id %in% ids)
  d9 <- pN |> filter(method == 'E7cr2')
  d10 <- pN |> filter(method == 'E7null_cr2')
  dF <- pN |> filter(method == 'F1')
  n_bn <- rvN_m$reps_null
  setv('bn_cpb', sprintf('%.1f', unique(nN$c_pb)))
  setv('bn_n', fn(n_bn))
  setv('bn_band', band_txt(n_bn))
  setv('bn_cells', length(ids))
  setv('bn_g9_d', rng(d9$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_g10_d', rng(d10$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_f1_d', rng(dF$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_g9_z', sprintf('%.1f', min(d9$diff_vs_g8 / d9$paired_se)))
  claim(all(d9$diff_vs_g8 > 0),
        'Block N, c_pb > 0: G9 above G8 in every cell.')
  claim(all(abs(d10$diff_vs_g8) < 2 * d10$paired_se),
        'Block N, c_pb > 0: G10 within 2 paired SE of G8.')
  above <- function(m) {
    sum(nN$reject[nN$method == m & is.na(nN$h_fixed)] >
          band(n_bn)[2])
  }
  setv('bn_up_g8', above('E2cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_g9', above('E7cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_g10', above('E7null_cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_f1', above('F1'))
  claim(above('E7null_cr2') <= above('E2cr2'),
        'Block N: G10 exceeds the band in no more cells than G8.')
}
```

```{r values-gapC, include = FALSE}
if (has_gfC) {
  n_c <- gfC_m$n_reps
  n_l <- gfC_m$n_reps_large
  setv('c_n', fn(n_c))
  setv('c_band', band_txt(n_c))
  setv('l_n', fn(n_l))
  setv('l_band', band_txt(n_l))
  C1 <- gfC |>
    filter(sub == 'C1-ladder') |>
    mutate(path = case_when(c_pb > 0 ~ 'progpb',
                            c_tv > 0 ~ 'progtvconst',
                            c_bl > 0 ~ 'progbl'),
           strength = pmax(c_pb, c_tv, c_bl))
  c0 <- C1 |> filter(c_bm == 0)
  setv('c_nnull', length(unique(c0$cell_id)))
  setv('c_g9_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_g10_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('c_f1_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'F1']))
  claim(all(in_band(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7cr2'], n_c)),
        'Feasible grid: G9 null inside the band in every cell.')
  pb0 <- c0 |> filter(path == 'progpb')
  op0 <- c0 |> filter(path != 'progpb')
  setv('c_pb_g9_est', rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_pb_g10_est',
       rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7null_cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_pb_f1_est', rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  setv('c_op_g9_est', rng(op0$mean_est[op0$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  claim(max(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2']) <
          min(op0$mean_est[op0$method == 'E7cr2']),
        'G9 null estimate is more negative under c_pb than elsewhere.')
  claim(all(abs(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'F1']) <
              abs(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2'])),
        'F1 null estimate is nearer zero than G9 under c_pb.')
  a3 <- C1 |> filter(c_bm > 0, c_bm < 0.45)
  setv('c_bm_alt', sprintf('%.2f', unique(a3$c_bm)))
  pb3 <- a3 |> filter(path == 'progpb')
  op3 <- a3 |> filter(path != 'progpb')
  setv('c_pb_g9_pw', rng(pb3$reject[pb3$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_pb_f1_pw', rng(pb3$reject[pb3$method == 'F1']))
  setv('c_op_g9_pw', rng(op3$reject[op3$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_pb_g9_ae', rng(pb3$mean_est[pb3$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_op_g9_ae', rng(op3$mean_est[op3$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_f1_ae', rng(a3$mean_est[a3$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  if (has_ceil) {
    mx <- function(p) max(a3$strength[a3$path == p])
    setv('c_mx_pb', sprintf('%.2f', mx('progpb')))
    setv('c_mx_bl', sprintf('%.2f', mx('progbl')))
    setv('c_gap_pb', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.3') - mx('progpb')))
    setv('c_gap_bl', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3') - mx('progbl')))
  }
  C2 <- gfC |> filter(sub == 'C2-largeN')
  lg <- function(m, n_, cpb) {
    row1(C2, method == m, N == n_, c_pb == cpb)
  }
  setv('l_g9_45', f3(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g10_45', f3(lg('E7null_cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g8_45', f3(lg('E2cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g1_45', f3(lg('E1', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_f1_45', f3(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_f1a0_45', f3(lg('F1A0', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_fb_45', f3(lg('F1A0B', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_30', f3(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.3)$reject))
  setv('l_f1_30', f3(lg('F1', 280, 0.3)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_140', f3(lg('E7cr2', 140, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_70', f3(row1(C1, method == 'E7cr2', path == 'progpb',
                          strength == 0.45, c_bm == 0)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_est', fs2(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$mean_est))
  setv('l_f1_est', fs2(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$mean_est))
  setv('l_g9_k', f2(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$kappa))
  setv('l_f1_k', f2(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$kappa))
  claim(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject > band(n_l)[2],
        'Large N: G9 above the band at N = 280, c_pb = 0.45.')
  claim(in_band(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$reject, n_l) &&
          in_band(lg('F1A0B', 280, 0.45)$reject, n_l),
        'Large N: F1 and F1A0B inside the band at N = 280.')
  ff <- C2 |> filter(method %in% c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'))
  ff0 <- c0 |> filter(path == 'progpb',
                      method %in% c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'))
  claim(all(in_band(ff$reject, n_l)) && all(in_band(ff0$reject, n_c)),
        paste('The F-family stays inside the band under the',
              'placebo-response pathway at every N.'))
  claim(all(in_band(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7null_cr2'], n_c)),
        'Feasible grid: G10 null inside the band in every cell.')
  if (has_gfCa) {
    cid <- lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$cell_id
    pd <- paired_diff(gfC_all, cid, 'E7cr2', 'F1')
    setv('l_pd', fs3(pd[['diff']]))
    setv('l_pd_se', f3(pd[['se']]))
    pd2 <- paired_diff(gfC_all, cid, 'E7null_cr2', 'F1A0')
    setv('l_pd2', fs3(pd2[['diff']]))
    setv('l_pd2_se', f3(pd2[['se']]))
    claim(pd[['diff']] < -2 * pd[['se']],
          'Large N: F1 rejects less than G9 by over 2 paired SE.')
  }
}
```

```{r values-trend, include = FALSE}
if (has_rvT) {
  n_t <- rvT_m$reps_other
  tn <- function(m) row1(rvT, method == m, c_bm == 0)
  ta <- function(m) row1(rvT, method == m, c_bm == 0.45)
  setv('t_coef', sprintf('%.1f', unique(rvT$b_tv_trend)))
  setv('t_n', fn(n_t))
  setv('t_band', band_txt(n_t))
  setv('t_g8', f3(tn('E2cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_g9', f3(tn('E7cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_f1', f3(tn('F1')$reject))
  setv('t_g8_est', fs2(tn('E2cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_g9_est', fs2(tn('E7cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_f1_est', fs2(tn('F1')$mean_est))
  setv('t_g8_se', f2(tn('E2cr2')$emp_se))
  pf <- row1(rvTp, method == 'F1', grepl('cbm0.00', cell_id))
  p9 <- row1(rvTp, method == 'E7cr2', grepl('cbm0.00', cell_id))
  setv('t_f1_d', fs3(pf$diff_vs_g8))
  setv('t_f1_dse', f3(pf$paired_se))
  setv('t_g9_d', fs3(p9$diff_vs_g8))
  setv('t_g9_dse', f3(p9$paired_se))
  setv('t_g9_pw', f3(ta('E7cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_g9_aest', fs2(ta('E7cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_f1_pw', f3(ta('F1')$reject))
  claim(tn('E7cr2')$reject > band(n_t)[2],
        'Trend: G9 null above the band.')
  claim(in_band(tn('F1')$reject, n_t),
        'Trend: F1 null inside the band.')
  claim(tn('F1')$mean_est < tn('E2cr2')$mean_est &&
          tn('F1')$mean_est > 0,
        'Trend: F1 null estimate positive but below that of G8.')
  if (has_rvA) {
    r0 <- row1(rvA, method == 'E7cr2', t1half == 0.5, N == 70,
               c_bm == 0.45)
    setv('t_ref_pw', f3(r0$reject))
    setv('t_ref_est', fs2(r0$mean_est))
    claim(ta('E7cr2')$reject < r0$reject,
          'Trend: G9 power below the no-trend reference.')
  }
}
```

```{r values-gvf, include = FALSE}
if (has_s27) {
  t1 <- s27 |> filter(design != 'CO')
  setv('g_n', fn(s27_m$n_reps))
  setv('g_band', band_txt(s27_m$n_reps))
  nul <- t1 |> filter(c_bm == 0)
  setv('g_null_g10', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('g_null_f1a0', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1A0']))
  setv('g_null_fb', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1A0B']))
  setv('g_null_f1', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1']))
  co_f <- s27 |> filter(design == 'CO', grepl('^F', method))
  claim(all(is.na(co_f$reject)),
        'The F-family is not estimable under CO.')
  alt <- t1 |> filter(c_bm > 0)
  ratio <- function(d, m) {
    w <- alt |> filter(design == d, method %in% c(m, 'E7null_cr2')) |>
      select(cell_id, method, reject) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = reject)
    100 * mean(w[[m]]) / mean(w$E7null_cr2)
  }
  for (d in c('Hybrid', 'OLBDC')) {
    for (m in c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B')) {
      setv(paste0('g_r_', d, '_', m), sprintf('%.1f', ratio(d, m)))
    }
  }
  if (has_s27a) {
    pool <- function(d, m) {
      ids <- unique(alt$cell_id[alt$design == d])
      x <- vapply(ids, function(i) {
        paired_diff(s27_all, i, 'E7null_cr2', m)[c('diff', 'se')]
      }, numeric(2))
      c(diff = mean(x['diff', ]),
        se = sqrt(sum(x['se', ]^2)) / ncol(x), k = ncol(x))
    }
    for (d in c('Hybrid', 'OLBDC')) {
      for (m in c('F1', 'F1A0')) {
        p <- pool(d, m)
        setv(paste0('g_pd_', d, '_', m), fs3(p[['diff']]))
        setv(paste0('g_pse_', d, '_', m), f3(p[['se']]))
        setv('g_k', p[['k']])
      }
    }
  }
}
if (has_rvA) {
  a2 <- rvA |> filter(t1half == 2, c_bm == 0.45)
  setv('a_f1_pw', rng(a2$reject[a2$method == 'F1']))
  setv('a_g10_pw', rng(a2$reject[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('a_f1_est', rng(a2$mean_est[a2$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  setv('a_g10_est', rng(a2$mean_est[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2'], fs2))
  claim(all(a2$reject[a2$method == 'F1'] <
              a2$reject[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2']),
        'Block A, t1/2 = 2: F1 below G10 in power in every cell.')
}
```

```{r values-hist, include = FALSE}
if (has_st_h && has_re_h) {
  ref_h <- re_h |>
    filter(pathway == 'none', c_bm == 0.45, method == 'G9') |>
    select(N, ref = reject)
  hh <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, method == 'E7cr2',
           pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst')) |>
    left_join(ref_h, by = 'N') |>
    mutate(loss = ref - reject)
  setv('h_ref35', f3(ref_h$ref[ref_h$N == 35]))
  setv('h_ref70', f3(ref_h$ref[ref_h$N == 70]))
  setv('h_loss6', rng(100 * hh$loss[hh$strength == 0.6],
                      function(x) sprintf('%.0f', x)))
  setv('h_loss3', f3(max(abs(hh$loss[hh$strength == 0.3]))))
  nmeth <- length(unique(st_h$method))
  setv('h_nmeth', nmeth)
  lw <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst')) |>
    select(pathway, N, method, strength, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = strength, values_from = reject,
                names_prefix = 's')
  claim(all(lw$s0.6 < lw$s0.3),
        paste('Historical: every analysis lost power at strength 0.6',
              'on the placebo-response and natural-history pathways.'))
}
if (has_pdc) {
  ps <- pdc$summary
  pv <- function(p, s, cb, w) ps[[w]][ps$pathway == p &
                                        ps$strength == s &
                                        ps$c_bm == cb]
  setv('h_c_none', fs2(pv('none', 0, 0.45, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_c_pb6', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.6, 0.45, 'contrast_repaired')))
  setv('h_c_tv6',
       fs2(pv('progtvconst', 0.6, 0.45, 'contrast_repaired')))
  setv('h_c_pb3n', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.3, 0, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_c_pb6n', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.6, 0, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_eig_pb3', f3(pv('progpb', 0.3, 0.45, 'min_eigenvalue')))
  setv('h_npaths', max(ps$paths_repaired))
  six_pd <- ps |>
    filter((pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst') &
              strength == 0.6) |
             (pathway == 'progbl' & strength == 0.6 & c_bm == 0.45))
  claim(all(six_pd$paths_repaired == max(ps$paths_repaired)),
        'Historical: every infeasible cell is repaired on all paths.')
}
if (has_re_h) {
  w <- re_h |>
    select(cell_id, method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = reject)
  dmx <- max(abs(c(w$G9rs, w$G9re, w$G9rse) - rep(w$G9, 3)))
  setv('re_dmax', f3(dmx))
  setv('re_ncell', nrow(w))
```

# Abstract {-}

**Background.** The biomarker-treatment interaction test of an
aggregated N-of-1 trial is built for a predictive biomarker. A
biomarker can also be prognostic. It can then be associated with the
natural history, the placebo response or the baseline level. We asked
when such an association biases the interaction test, and what
removes the bias.

**Methods.** We simulated the Hybrid design under the extended
data-generating process (DGP) of the companion paper, with the
parameter values published by Hendrickson et al. Five prognostic
pathways were examined. Three are correlations of the biomarker with a
component. Two are mean shifts of the natural-history component, one
constant and one growing over the trial. We compared analyses with
and without the design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$.

**Results.** Under a correlation with the placebo-response component
of 0.45, the analyses without expectancy terms rejected a true null at
`r V('l_g9_45')` (G9) at $N = 280$. With the terms, the rate was
`r V('l_f1_45')` (F1). The two-MCSE band at `r V('l_n')` replicates
was `r V('l_band')`.
Under a natural-history shift that grows over the trial, G9 rejected
at `r V('t_g9')` and F1 at `r V('t_f1')` at $N = 70$. Without a
prognostic effect, F1A0 reached `r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0')` percent of
the power of G10 in the Hybrid cells. The power loss once attributed
to a strong prognostic correlation came from repaired covariance
matrices. Under the current stop on infeasible matrices, all
`r V('n6_refused')` of those cells were refused.

**Conclusions.** For a biomarker that may be prognostic, add
$\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$ to the recommended analysis of the
companion paper. A biomarker that may predict the rate of
natural-history change needs a biomarker-by-time term. That remedy
has not yet been simulated.

# Notation and glossary {-}

Symbols follow `analysis/report/NOTATION.md`. Two symbols are not yet
listed there and are marked *proposed*.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $B_i$, $B^c_i$ | biomarker of participant $i$; centered at the trial's baseline mean |
| $z_i$ | standardized biomarker |
| $w_t$ | calendar week of visit $t$ |
| $c_{bm}$ | on-drug biomarker-response correlation, the interaction under the correlation encoding |
| $c_{bm,PB}$, $c_{bm,TV}$, $c_{bm,BL}$ | prognostic correlations of the biomarker with the placebo-response component, the natural-history component and the baseline level |
| $b_{TV}$ (*proposed*) | constant natural-history mean shift per SD of the biomarker |
| $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ (*proposed*) | coefficient of the trend pathway: a shift of $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i\,g(w_t)$, with $g$ the natural-history mean course scaled to peak 1 |
| $\sigma_{BR}$, $\sigma_{PB}$, $\sigma_{TV}$ | SDs of the drug-response, placebo-response and natural-history components |
| $t_{1/2}$, $t^a_{1/2}$ | carryover half-life of the DGP; half-life assumed by the analysis |
| $D_{bc,it}$ | exposure-weighted drug indicator built at $t^a_{1/2}$ |
| $\eta_t$ | design expectancy: 1 open label, 0.5 blinded, 0 at baseline |
| $\beta_{bm:D}$ | interaction coefficient, the target of the test |
| $\beta_\eta$, $\beta_{bm:\eta}$ | coefficients of $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$ |
| $\kappa$ | mean model standard error divided by the empirical SD of the estimates |
| $\hat\pi$, MCSE | estimated rejection rate and its Monte Carlo standard error |

- **Correlation encoding.** The interaction is a correlation between
  the biomarker and the drug response. It is present on drug and
  decays after discontinuation at the carryover half-life. Code
  labels it `mvn`.
- **Original DGP; extended DGP.** The original DGP is the code
  published by Hendrickson et al. at commit `58b32a9`
  [@hendrickson2020]. The extended DGP is the one recommended in
  paper 01 [@pmsimstats-paper01]. It has a decaying biomarker-response
  correlation, the same first-order autoregressive correlation for
  every component with a constant between-component correlation at
  every lag ($\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$), carryover that decays from
  the last on-drug mean, and a stop on correlation matrices that are
  not positive definite. Code and data label it `refined`.
- **Published parameter set; simcore2026 set.** The published set is
  the component means and SDs of Hendrickson et al. The simcore2026
  set is an earlier set used by the paper 02 drivers before
  2026-11-03. Runs under it are labeled historical in this draft.
- **Predictive biomarker.** One that changes the drug response
  ($c_{bm} \ne 0$). **Prognostic biomarker:** one associated with the
  outcome through another channel. A biomarker can be both.
- **Prognostic pathway.** One channel of prognostic association. The
  stored data labels are `prog-BL` ($c_{bm,BL}$), `prog-TV-const`
  ($c_{bm,TV}$), `prog-PB` ($c_{bm,PB}$), `prog-TV-grow` ($b_{TV}$,
  constant despite its label) and the block T trend pathway
  ($b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}$).
- **Feasibility bound.** The largest value of one correlation, given
  the others, for which the joint correlation matrix is positive
  definite on every path of the design.
- **Silent repair; repaired cell.** Before 2026-10-26 the drivers
  replaced a matrix that was not positive definite with a nearby one
  that was, without warning. A repaired cell is a cell simulated
  under such a matrix.
- **G-family.** Analyses with no expectancy terms. **G8:**
  $D_{bc,it}$ at the true half-life with CR2, an oracle benchmark and
  not a candidate analysis. **G9:** $t^a_{1/2}$ chosen by AIC on the
  model with the interaction, with CR2. **G10:** $t^a_{1/2}$ chosen by
  AIC on the model without the interaction, the interaction model
  refitted, with CR2. G10 is the recommended analysis of paper 02
  [@pmsimstats-paper02]. G1 and G6 are the binary-indicator analyses,
  model-based and with CR2. Stored codes: `E2cr2`, `E7cr2`,
  `E7null_cr2`, `E1`, `E1cr2`.
- **F-family.** The G3 formula plus $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$, with
  CR2. **F1:** $t^a_{1/2}$ fixed at the half-life policy value of 0.2
  week. **F1A:** chosen by AIC with the interaction in the model.
  **F1A0:** chosen by AIC without it. **F1A0B:** F1A0 with a
  single-resample parametric-bootstrap calibration that repeats the
  selection.
- **CR2.** The Bell-McCaffrey bias-reduced cluster-robust standard
  error with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
  [@bell2002bias; @pustejovsky2018].
- **Two-MCSE band.** The interval $0.05 \pm 2\sqrt{0.05 \times
  0.95/n}$ at $n$ replicates.
- **Designs.** Hybrid: open-label titration, then blinded
  discontinuation, then a brief crossover. OL+BDC: open-label
  titration then blinded discontinuation. CO: a two-period crossover.
- **Single-resample bootstrap.** One bootstrap resample per Monte
  Carlo replicate, with the critical value taken from the pooled
  resamples of the cell.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

An aggregated N-of-1 trial gives each participant repeated periods on
and off drug. Pooling the participants allows a test of whether a
baseline biomarker modifies the drug effect. That test targets a
predictive biomarker. The interaction test in a parallel-group trial
already needs a large sample [@brookes2004]. The N-of-1 design
reduces that cost by comparing each participant with themselves
[@senn2002; @araujo2016].

A biomarker can also be prognostic. It may track the severity at
baseline, the natural course of the illness, or the response to
placebo. In a design whose expectancy varies between open-label and
blinded phases, the on-drug and off-drug visits differ in more than
drug exposure. A prognostic association that differs between those
visits can then project onto the interaction term. The test would
then report moderation of the drug effect where there is none.

The companion paper on carryover [@pmsimstats-paper02] studies a
predictive-only biomarker. It recommends G10. That analysis uses an
exposure-weighted drug indicator, chooses its half-life by AIC on the
model without the interaction, and tests with CR2. This paper asks
what changes when the biomarker is also prognostic. It examines five
pathways. It compares the G-family with the F-family, which adds the
design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$. It also reports
a finding about the simulation itself. An apparent loss of power
under a strong prognostic correlation came from the silent repair of
infeasible covariance matrices. It was not a property of any
analysis.

The data-generating facts are established in paper 01
[@pmsimstats-paper01]. A prognostic correlation shares one
feasibility condition with $c_{bm}$. The extended DGP refuses a
matrix that is not positive definite. This paper cites those results
and reports only their consequences for the analysis. The studies are
exploratory.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Data-generating process {#sec-dgp}

All published-set cells use the extended DGP under the correlation
encoding, on the Hybrid design, with $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week unless
stated. The component means and SDs are those of Hendrickson et al.
Table \@ref(tab:tab-params) reads them from the stored run metadata.
The drug-response SD is $\sigma_{BR} =$ `r V('sig_br')`. The true
interaction at $c_{bm}$ is therefore $-c_{bm}\sigma_{BR}$ per SD of
the biomarker: `r V('truth45')` at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ and
`r V('truth30')` at $c_{bm} = 0.30$. The components are reductions in
symptom severity, so an increase in any component lowers the
outcome. Interaction coefficients are negative.

```{r tab-params}
pm <- if (!is.null(gfC_m)) gfC_m else st_p_m
if (!is.null(pm$params$resp_param)) {
  rp <- pm$params$resp_param
  bp <- pm$params$baseline_param
  cat_lab <- c(tv = 'Natural history (TV)', pb = 'Placebo response (PB)',
               br = 'Drug response (BR)', bm = 'Biomarker',
               BL = 'Baseline level')
  tp <- rbind(
    data.frame(Component = cat_lab[rp$cat],
               Mean = sprintf('%.2f', rp$max),
               SD = sprintf('%g', rp$sd),
               Rate = sprintf('%.2f', rp$rate),
               Displacement = sprintf('%g', rp$disp)),
    data.frame(Component = cat_lab[bp$cat],
               Mean = sprintf('%.1f', bp$m),
               SD = sprintf('%.1f', bp$sd),
               Rate = '--', Displacement = '--'))
  rownames(tp) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(tp, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c('Component', 'Maximum or mean', 'SD',
                  'Rate (per week)', 'Displacement'),
    caption = 'Parameter values of the published-set runs, read from
      the stored run metadata (\\texttt{meta.rds}, field
      \\texttt{params}). For the
      response components the mean column is the maximum $m$ of the
      modified Gompertz curve.') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the parameter table of the published-set runs')
}
```

## Prognostic pathways {#sec-pathways}

A biomarker may be associated with the outcome through channels other
than the drug response. Three pathways are entries in the biomarker
row of the joint correlation matrix. Each sets one correlation with
the others at zero. The first is a correlation with the baseline
level, $c_{bm,BL}$. The second is a correlation with the
natural-history component at every visit, $c_{bm,TV}$. The third is a
correlation with the placebo-response component at every visit,
$c_{bm,PB}$. Their strengths are bounded by feasibility (Section
\@ref(sec-feasibility)).

Two further pathways are mean shifts. They are not bounded by the
correlation matrix. The constant shift adds $b_{TV}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i$
to the natural-history mean at every visit. It is stored as
`prog-TV-grow` although it does not grow. It is absorbed exactly by
the biomarker main effect of every analysis here (Appendix
\@ref(sec-absorb)). It serves only as a check of that absorption. The
trend pathway adds $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i\,g(w_t)$,
where $g$ is the natural-history mean course scaled to peak 1. It
describes a biomarker that predicts the rate of natural-history
change. A model with no biomarker-by-time term cannot absorb it.

## Analyses {#sec-analyses}

All analyses fit a linear mixed model with a participant random
intercept and continuous-time AR(1) residual correlation
(`corCAR1`). The G-family model is
$$
Y_{it} = \beta_0 + \beta_B B^c_i + \beta_T w_t + \beta_D D_{bc,it}
  + \beta_{bm:D} B^c_i D_{bc,it} + u_i + \epsilon_{it}.
$$
$D_{bc,it}$ is one on drug, $2^{-t_{sd}/t^a_{1/2}}$ off drug after
first exposure, and zero before first exposure. G8 sets
$t^a_{1/2} = t_{1/2}$. It is an oracle benchmark and not a candidate
analysis. G9 chooses $t^a_{1/2}$ by maximum-likelihood AIC over
$\{0.25, 0.5, 1, 2\}$ weeks with the interaction in the model
[@akaike1974new]. G10 makes the same choice on the model without the
interaction and refits the interaction model by REML. The selection
of G9 depends on the coefficient under test. That is a
post-selection inference risk [@berk2013valid; @leeb2005]. All three
test $\beta_{bm:D}$ with CR2 and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

The F-family adds the design-expectancy terms:
$$
Y_{it} = \ldots + \beta_\eta \eta_t + \beta_{bm:\eta} B^c_i \eta_t.
$$
The regressors are `De` and `bmc:De`. The placebo-response amplitude
scales with $\eta_t$, and $\eta_t$ differs between on-drug and
off-drug visits in the Hybrid design. A biomarker correlated with the
placebo response therefore acquires an on/off slope difference by
construction. The term $B^c_i\eta_t$ absorbs it. F1 fixes
$t^a_{1/2}$ at 0.2 week. F1A selects it by AIC with the interaction.
F1A0 selects it without the interaction, as G10 does. F1A0B
calibrates F1A0 by a single-resample parametric bootstrap under the
null that repeats the selection. Its candidate grid is $\{0, 0.2,
0.5, 1, 2\}$ weeks. $\eta_t$ is constant within every path of the
crossover design. The F-family is therefore not estimable under CO.
F1A0 and G10 differ only in the expectancy terms. That is the
property that lets papers 02 and 15 give one recommendation
(Section \@ref(sec-recommend)).

## Performance measures {#sec-perf}

We report the rejection rate $\hat\pi$ at $\alpha = 0.05$, its MCSE,
the mean interaction estimate, and $\kappa$ [@morris2019simulation].
Under the null $\hat\pi$ is the Type I error. A cell's rejection rate
is compared with its two-MCSE band. That band is a check on gross
departures and not a demonstration of nominal size. Within a job,
cells at the same design and $N$ share random-number streams, and
every analysis is fitted to the same trials. Contrasts between
analyses are paired, and their standard errors come from the
per-replicate rejection indicators. Comparisons across jobs are
unpaired. Results from different simulation hosts are not
draw-for-draw identical.

## Stored runs and their parameter sets {#sec-sources}

Table \@ref(tab:tab-sources) lists every stored run this draft reads.
The published-set runs are the reruns of `docs/74`. The historical
runs used the simcore2026 parameter set and silent repair. They are
kept only as the exhibit of Section \@ref(sec-artifact)
(`docs/74`, decision D5). No historical number enters a result about
an analysis.

```{r tab-sources}
srow <- function(what, folder, meta, kind) {
  data.frame(
    Run = what,
    Folder = paste0('\\texttt{', gsub('_', '\\\\_', folder), '}'),
    Set = if (is.null(meta)) 'missing' else param_set(meta),
    Date = if (is.null(meta) || is.null(meta$date)) '--' else
      format(as.Date(meta$date)),
    Kind = kind)
}
tsrc <- rbind(
  srow('Prognostic stress test', 'published/g9-prognostic-stress',
       st_p_m, 'published set'),
  srow('Feasible grid and large N', 'published/g9-gap-fill/C',

  srow('Hybrid alternatives (block A)',
       'published/referee-variants/block-A', rvA_m, 'published set'),

  srow('Random-slope variants', 'g9-random-effects', re_h_m,

knitr::kable(tsrc, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
  col.names = c('Run', 'Folder under carryover-sensitivity/',
                'Parameter set recorded', 'Date', 'Status'),
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Feasibility of a prognostic correlation {#sec-feasibility}

Paper 01 derives the joint feasibility condition and tabulates the
bounds for every design [@pmsimstats-paper01]. A prognostic
correlation occupies the same biomarker row of the correlation
matrix as $c_{bm}$. The two share one condition, a quadratic form in
the correlations that must be below one. We do not repeat that
table. We quote only the bounds at this paper's configuration:
Hybrid, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, $\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$. The bounds
depend on the correlation matrix only, not on the component SDs. They
therefore hold for both parameter sets.

Alone, $c_{bm}$ is feasible up to `r V('b_bm')` and $c_{bm,PB}$ or
$c_{bm,TV}$ up to `r V('b_pb')`. Given $c_{bm} = 0.30$ the bound on
$c_{bm,PB}$ or $c_{bm,TV}$ is `r V('b_pb30')` and on $c_{bm,BL}$ is
`r V('b_bl30')`. Given $c_{bm} = 0.45$ they are `r V('b_pb45')` and
`r V('b_bl45')`. No $c_{bm}$ is feasible with $c_{bm,PB}$ or
$c_{bm,TV}$ at 0.6. Strength 0.3 therefore lies just inside the
bound at $c_{bm} = 0.45$. Strength 0.6 is infeasible at every
$c_{bm}$ on those two pathways. The feasible grid of Section
\@ref(sec-grid) was chosen from these bounds.

## Correlation pathways at strength 0.3 {#sec-stress}

We crossed the three correlation pathways and the constant shift
with $c_{bm} \in \{0, 0.45\}$ and $N \in \{35, 70\}$, at
`r V('st_n')` replicates per cell. Table \@ref(tab:tab-stress) gives
the rejection rates. The two-MCSE band is `r V('st_band')`.

```{r tab-stress}
if (has_st_p) {
  ts <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, method %in% show_m) |>
    mutate(Pathway = path_lab[pathway], Method = m_lab[method]) |>
    select(pathway, Pathway, c_bm, N, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    arrange(match(pathway, path_ord), c_bm, N) |>
    select(Pathway, c_bm, N, all_of(show_c)) |>
    mutate(c_bm = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
           across(all_of(show_c), f3))
  ts$Pathway[duplicated(ts$Pathway)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(ts, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Pathway', '$c_{bm}$', '$N$', show_c),
    caption = sprintf('Rejection rate under each prognostic pathway
      at strength 0.3, published parameter set. Hybrid, $t_{1/2} =
      0.5$ week, %s replicates per cell, the same trials for every
      analysis. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ are Type I error (band %s).
      G8 is the oracle benchmark.', V('st_n'), V('st_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set prognostic stress test')
}
```

The G9 Type I error was `r V('st_g9_null')` across the six null cells
of the three correlation pathways. G10 gave `r V('st_g10_null')` and
F1A0B `r V('st_fb_null')`. Every G9 and G10 null rate was inside the
band. The G9 power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ was `r V('st_g9_alt')`. The
no-confound reference from block A of the referee-variant runs is
`r V('ref35')` at $N = 35$ and `r V('ref70')` at $N = 70$. The
largest difference from it was `r V('st_g9_dmax')`, under the
placebo-response pathway. Section \@ref(sec-grid) shows that this
excess is bias in the estimate. That comparison is
unpaired, against `r V('a_n')`-replicate cells of another job. F1A0B
differed from G10 in power by `r V('st_fb_g10')` on the same trials.
The constant shift gave the same rejection at strengths 0.3 and 0.6
in every analysis. In the scenario job, the constant-shift null cell
differs from the unshifted Hybrid null cell by at most
`r V('abs_dd')` in any analysis. That is the absorption of Appendix
\@ref(sec-absorb).

A longer run at the placebo-response pathway sharpens the size
comparison. Block N of the referee-variant runs fitted G8, G9, G10
and F1 to `r V('bn_n')` replicates in each of `r V('bn_cells')`
Hybrid null cells at $c_{bm,PB} =$ `r V('bn_cpb')`
(Table \@ref(tab:tab-blockN)). The band is `r V('bn_band')`. The
paired difference from G8 was `r V('bn_g9_d')` for G9, `r V('bn_g10_d')`
for G10 and `r V('bn_f1_d')` for F1. G9 was above G8 in every cell,
by at least `r V('bn_g9_z')` paired standard errors. G10 was within
two paired standard errors of G8 in every cell. The number of cells
above the band was `r V('bn_up_g8')` for G8, `r V('bn_up_g9')` for
G9, `r V('bn_up_g10')` for G10 and `r V('bn_up_f1')` for F1.

```{r tab-blockN}
if (has_rvN) {
  tb <- rvN |>
    filter(c_pb > 0, is.na(h_fixed)) |>
    left_join(rvNp |> select(cell_id, method, h_fixed, diff_vs_g8,
                             paired_se),
              by = c('cell_id', 'method', 'h_fixed')) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = sprintf('$t_{1/2} = %.1f$, $N = %d$', t1half, N)) |>
    arrange(t1half, N, match(method, show_m)) |>
    transmute(Cell, Method,
              Rejection = sprintf('%.4f (%.4f)', reject, mcse),
              `Diff. vs G8 (SE)` = ifelse(is.na(diff_vs_g8), '--',
                sprintf('%+.4f (%.4f)', diff_vs_g8, paired_se)),
              `$\\kappa$` = f2(kappa))
  tb$Cell[duplicated(tb$Cell)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(tb, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Block N, published parameter set: null
      rejection rate (MCSE) under the placebo-response pathway at
      $c_{bm,PB} = %s$, Hybrid, %s replicates per cell, the same
      trials for every analysis, with the paired difference from G8
      and its paired SE. Band %s.', V('bn_cpb'), V('bn_n'),
      V('bn_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 8)
} else {
  pending_note('block N of the published-set referee-variant runs')
}
```

## The feasible prognostic grid {#sec-grid}

The supplementary study ran a grid of correlations chosen inside the
feasibility bounds. At $c_{bm} = 0.30$ it set $c_{bm,PB}$ and
$c_{bm,TV}$ at 0.40 and 0.45, and $c_{bm,BL}$ at 0.6 and 0.8. It also
ran $c_{bm,BL} = 0.45$ at $c_{bm} = 0.45$. Each cell was run with and
without a true interaction, at $N = 70$ and `r V('c_n')` replicates.
The strongest $c_{bm,PB}$ lies `r V('c_gap_pb')` below its bound at
$c_{bm} = 0.30$. The strongest $c_{bm,BL}$ lies `r V('c_gap_bl')`
below its bound. Table \@ref(tab:tab-grid) gives the rejection rates
and Table \@ref(tab:tab-grid-est) the mean estimates.

```{r tab-grid}
if (has_gfC) {
  tg <- C1 |>
    filter(method %in% show_m) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = sprintf('%s = %.2f, $c_{bm} = %.2f$',
                          path_lab[path], strength, c_bm)) |>
    arrange(match(path, path_ord), strength, c_bm) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    select(Cell, all_of(show_c)) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tg, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Rejection rate on the feasible prognostic grid,
      published parameter set. Hybrid, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$
      week, %s replicates per cell. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ are Type I
      error (band %s). The others are power.', V('c_n'),
      V('c_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set feasible prognostic grid')
}
```

```{r tab-grid-est}
if (has_gfC) {
  te <- C1 |>
    filter(method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0')) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Truth = -c_bm * sigma_br,
           Cell = sprintf('%s = %.2f, $c_{bm} = %.2f$',
                          path_lab[path], strength, c_bm)) |>
    arrange(match(path, path_ord), strength, c_bm) |>
    select(Cell, Truth, Method, mean_est) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = mean_est) |>
    select(Cell, Truth, G9, G10, F1, F1A0) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, fs2))
  knitr::kable(te, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = 'Mean interaction estimate on the feasible prognostic
      grid (same cells as the rejection table). The true value is
      $-c_{bm}\\sigma_{BR}$ per SD of the biomarker.') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set feasible prognostic grid')
}
```

The G9 Type I error was `r V('c_g9_null')` across the
`r V('c_nnull')` null cells, inside the band in every one. G10 gave
`r V('c_g10_null')` and F1 `r V('c_f1_null')`. The rejection rates
hide a bias that the mean estimates show. Under the placebo-response
pathway with no true interaction, the mean G9 estimate was
`r V('c_pb_g9_est')`. G10 gave `r V('c_pb_g10_est')`. F1 gave
`r V('c_pb_f1_est')`. Under the other two pathways the mean G9
estimate was `r V('c_op_g9_est')`. At $c_{bm} =$ `r V('c_bm_alt')`
the same bias appears as excess power. G9 reached `r V('c_pb_g9_pw')`
under the placebo-response pathway and `r V('c_op_g9_pw')` under the
others. Its mean estimate was `r V('c_pb_g9_ae')` and
`r V('c_op_g9_ae')` against a true value of `r V('truth30')`. F1
reached `r V('c_pb_f1_pw')` under the placebo-response pathway. Its
mean estimate was `r V('c_f1_ae')` across the grid. The F1 estimate
is attenuated because its fixed half-life of 0.2 week is below the
true 0.5 week (Section \@ref(sec-gvf)). The excess power of the
G-family under the placebo-response pathway is therefore not evidence
of better power. It is the same bias as under the null.

## Larger samples under the placebo-response pathway {#sec-largen}

A bias of a fixed size becomes Type I error inflation as $N$ grows,
because the standard error shrinks. The supplementary study ran the
placebo-response pathway with no true interaction at $N \in \{140,
280\}$ and $c_{bm,PB} \in \{0.30, 0.45\}$, at `r V('l_n')`
replicates. The band is `r V('l_band')`. Table \@ref(tab:tab-largen)
gives the result.

```{r tab-largen}
if (has_gfC) {
  tl <- gfC |>
    filter(sub == 'C2-largeN' |
             (sub == 'C1-ladder' & c_pb == 0.45 & c_bm == 0)) |>
    filter(method %in% c('E1', show_m)) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = sprintf('$c_{bm,PB} = %.2f$, $N = %d$', c_pb, N)) |>
    arrange(c_pb, N) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    select(Cell, G1, all_of(show_c)) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tl, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Type I error under the placebo-response
      pathway at larger samples, published parameter set. Hybrid,
      $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, $c_{bm} = 0$, %s replicates at $N = 140$
      and $280$ (band %s). The $N = 70$ row is from the feasible grid
      at %s replicates.', V('l_n'), V('l_band'), V('c_n'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set large-sample cells')
}
```

At $N = 280$ and $c_{bm,PB} = 0.45$, G9 rejected at
`r V('l_g9_45')`, G10 at `r V('l_g10_45')` and G8 at `r V('l_g8_45')`.
The model-based binary-indicator analysis G1 rejected at
`r V('l_g1_45')`. The F-family stayed inside the band: F1 at
`r V('l_f1_45')`, F1A0 at `r V('l_f1a0_45')` and F1A0B at
`r V('l_fb_45')`. On the same trials, the paired difference in
rejection of F1 minus G9 was `r V('l_pd')` (paired SE
`r V('l_pd_se')`). That of F1A0 minus G10 was `r V('l_pd2')`
(`r V('l_pd2_se')`). The G9 rate rose with $N$:
`r V('l_g9_70')` at 70, `r V('l_g9_140')` at 140 and
`r V('l_g9_45')` at 280. Its mean estimate at $N = 280$ was
`r V('l_g9_est')` against `r V('l_f1_est')` for F1. The standard
errors were calibrated for both, with $\kappa$ of `r V('l_g9_k')` and
`r V('l_f1_k')`. The excess is therefore bias, not an
underestimated standard error. At $c_{bm,PB} = 0.30$ the rates were
`r V('l_g9_30')` for G9 and `r V('l_f1_30')` for F1.

## The trend pathway {#sec-trend}

Block T of the referee-variant runs simulated a natural-history shift
that grows over the trial, with $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}} =$
`r V('t_coef')`. It is a mean shift, so the feasibility bound does
not limit it. G8, G9 and F1 were fitted at $N = 70$ and
`r V('t_n')` replicates (Table \@ref(tab:tab-trend)). The band is
`r V('t_band')`.

```{r tab-trend}
if (has_rvT) {
  tt <- rvT |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = ifelse(c_bm == 0, 'null ($c_{bm} = 0$)',
                         sprintf('$c_{bm} = %.2f$', c_bm))) |>
    arrange(c_bm, match(method, show_m)) |>
    transmute(Cell, Method,
              Rejection = sprintf('%.3f (%.3f)', reject, mcse),
              `Mean estimate` = fs2(mean_est),
              `Empirical SE` = f2(emp_se),
              `$\\kappa$` = f2(kappa))
  tt$Cell[duplicated(tt$Cell)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(tt, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Block T, published parameter set: rejection
      rate (MCSE), mean interaction estimate, empirical SE and
      calibration ratio under the trend pathway
      ($b_{TV}^{\\mathrm{tr}} = %s$). Hybrid, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} =
      0.5$ week, %s replicates. The true value is 0 at the null and
      %s at $c_{bm} = 0.45$. Band at the null %s.', V('t_coef'),
      V('t_n'), V('truth45'), V('t_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('block T of the published-set referee-variant runs')
}
```

The trend pathway biased the G-family. Under the null G8 rejected at
`r V('t_g8')` and G9 at `r V('t_g9')`. Their mean estimates were
`r V('t_g8_est')` and `r V('t_g9_est')` where the truth is zero. The
G8 empirical SE was `r V('t_g8_se')`. F1 rejected at `r V('t_f1')`,
with a mean estimate of `r V('t_f1_est')`. Paired against G8, F1
differed by `r V('t_f1_d')` (SE `r V('t_f1_dse')`) and G9 by
`r V('t_g9_d')` (`r V('t_g9_dse')`). The expectancy terms therefore
absorb part of the shift but not all of it. At $c_{bm} = 0.45$ the
bias is toward zero. G9 power was `r V('t_g9_pw')` with a mean
estimate of `r V('t_g9_aest')`. In the no-trend cell of block A it
was `r V('t_ref_pw')` with `r V('t_ref_est')`. That comparison is
unpaired. The mechanism is the design. In the Hybrid design
$D_{bc,it}$ falls with calendar time, so a biomarker that predicts
the trend projects onto the interaction term of a model with no
biomarker-by-time term.

## The biomarker-by-time remedy: RESULTS PENDING {#sec-bmt}

\fbox{\parbox{0.95\linewidth}{\textbf{RESULTS PENDING.} The
simulation for this section has not been run. This section contains
no results. It will be written from the block described in the split
plan, Section 3.1, once that block is stored.}}

The remedy adds a biomarker-by-time term $B^c_i w_t$ to the analysis
model, as `bmc:t`. Its coefficient would be written
$\beta_{bm:T}$ (*proposed*). A quadratic variant adds $B^c_i w_t^2$.
The planned block crosses the trend pathway, present or absent, with
a null and an alternative interaction. It fits G8, G9, G10 and F1A0
with and without the term to the same trials. It answers three
questions. Does the term remove the trend bias in size and in the
mean estimate? What does it cost in power when there is no trend?
Does a linear term suffice when the natural-history course is not a
straight line? The driver changes it needs are listed in the
Reproducibility section.

## Expectancy terms without a prognostic effect {#sec-gvf}

The F-family's cost when the biomarker is predictive only was
measured on the original 30-cell grid of paper 02 under the published
parameter set (`r V('g_n')` replicates per cell). The F-family is
not estimable under CO, so only the Hybrid and OL+BDC cells enter.
Table \@ref(tab:tab-gvf) gives the rejection rates.

```{r tab-gvf}
if (has_s27) {
  tv <- s27 |>
    filter(design != 'CO',
           method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0',
                         'F1A0B')) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Design = ifelse(design == 'OLBDC', 'OL+BDC', design)) |>
    arrange(Design, c_bm, t1half, N) |>
    select(Design, c_bm, t1half, N, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    select(Design, c_bm, t1half, N, G9, G10, F1, F1A0, F1A0B) |>
    mutate(c_bm = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
           t1half = sprintf('%.1f', t1half),
           across(c(G9, G10, F1, F1A0, F1A0B), f3))
  tv$Design[duplicated(tv$Design)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(tv, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Design', '$c_{bm}$', '$t_{1/2}$', '$N$', 'G9',
                  'G10', 'F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'),
    caption = sprintf('Original 30-cell grid of paper 02, published
      parameter set, Hybrid and OL+BDC cells: rejection rate with no
      prognostic effect. %s replicates per cell, the same trials for
      every analysis. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ are Type I error (band
      %s).', V('g_n'), V('g_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set original grid')
}
```

The null rates were `r V('g_null_g10')` for G10, `r V('g_null_f1a0')`
for F1A0, `r V('g_null_fb')` for F1A0B and `r V('g_null_f1')` for F1.
Over the alternative cells of the Hybrid design, F1A0 reached
`r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0')` percent of the mean power of G10, F1A0B
`r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0B')` percent and F1 `r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1')`
percent. Under OL+BDC the figures were `r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1A0')`,
`r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1A0B')` and `r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1')` percent. The mean
paired difference from G10 over the `r V('g_k')` Hybrid alternative
cells was `r V('g_pd_Hybrid_F1A0')` for F1A0 (SE
`r V('g_pse_Hybrid_F1A0')`) and `r V('g_pd_Hybrid_F1')` for F1
(`r V('g_pse_Hybrid_F1')`). Under OL+BDC it was
`r V('g_pd_OLBDC_F1A0')` (`r V('g_pse_OLBDC_F1A0')`) and
`r V('g_pd_OLBDC_F1')` (`r V('g_pse_OLBDC_F1')`). The pooled
standard errors treat the cells as independent. Cells at the same
$N$ share random-number streams, so they are approximate.

F1 also loses power where its fixed half-life is wrong. In block A
at a true half-life of 2 weeks and $c_{bm} = 0.45$, F1 reached
`r V('a_f1_pw')` against `r V('a_g10_pw')` for G10. Its mean estimate
was `r V('a_f1_est')` against `r V('a_g10_est')` for G10 and a true
value of `r V('truth45')`. The fixed half-life is the cost, not the
expectancy terms. F1A0, which selects the half-life, is the fair
comparator for the terms themselves.

```{r tab-scen}
if (has_s21) {
  sc_lab <- c(hybrid_null = 'Hybrid, null',
              olbdc_null = 'OL+BDC, null',
              t1hifhi_null = '$t_{1/2} = 2$ wk, null',
              shapemis_null = 'Weibull $k = 2$ data, null',
              hybrid_alt = 'Hybrid, $c_{bm} = 0.45$',
              hybrid_alt_lo = 'Hybrid, $c_{bm} = 0.25$',
              olbdc_alt = 'OL+BDC, $c_{bm} = 0.45$',
              t1hifhi_alt = '$t_{1/2} = 2$ wk, $c_{bm} = 0.25$',
              shapemis_alt = 'Weibull $k = 2$ data, $c_{bm} = 0.25$')
  tsc <- s21 |>
    filter(cell %in% names(sc_lab),
           method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0',
                         'F1A0B')) |>
    mutate(Cell = sc_lab[cell], Method = m_lab[method]) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    arrange(match(Cell, sc_lab)) |>
    select(Cell, G9, G10, F1, F1A0, F1A0B) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tsc, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Scenario cells of paper 02, published parameter
      set, no prognostic effect: rejection rate. Hybrid unless
      stated, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week unless stated, %s
      replicates. In the $t_{1/2} = 2$ week rows the fixed half-life
      of F1 is a tenth of the true value.', fn(s21_m$n_reps))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set scenario cells')
}
```

## The repair artifact: a historical exhibit {#sec-artifact}

\fbox{\parbox{0.95\linewidth}{\textbf{Historical exhibit.} Every
number in this section comes from runs under the simcore2026 parameter
set with silent repair (Table \ref{tab:tab-sources}). They are
evidence about a repaired DGP. They are not evidence about any
analysis under a prognostic biomarker.}}

The first prognostic stress test ran at strengths 0.3 and 0.6 before
the drivers refused infeasible matrices. At strength 0.6 on the
placebo-response and natural-history pathways, G9 lost
`r V('h_loss6')` points of power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ against the
no-confound reference of `r V('h_ref35')` ($N = 35$) and
`r V('h_ref70')` ($N = 70$). At strength 0.3 the largest loss was
`r V('h_loss3')`. Every one of the `r V('h_nmeth')` analyses fitted
to the same trials lost power at strength 0.6 (Table
\@ref(tab:tab-hist)). That uniformity was the first sign that the
loss arose before the analysis.

```{r tab-hist}
if (has_st_h) {
  th <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, method %in% c('E7cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0B'),
           pathway != 'progtvgrow') |>
    mutate(Pathway = path_lab[pathway], Method = m_lab[method]) |>
    select(pathway, Pathway, N, strength, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(Method, strength), values_from = reject,
                names_sep = ' ') |>
    arrange(match(pathway, path_ord), N) |>
    select(Pathway, N, `G9 0.3`, `G9 0.6`, `F1 0.3`, `F1 0.6`,
           `F1A0B 0.3`, `F1A0B 0.6`) |>
    mutate(across(-c(Pathway, N), f3))
  th$Pathway[duplicated(th$Pathway)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(th, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Pathway', '$N$', rep(c('0.3', '0.6'), 3)),
    caption = sprintf('Historical exhibit (simcore2026 parameter set,
      silent repair): power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ at prognostic
      strengths 0.3 and 0.6, Hybrid, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, %s
      replicates. Every strength-0.6 cell here, including
      $c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$, was simulated under a repaired matrix.',
      fn(st_h_m$n_reps))) |>
    kableExtra::add_header_above(c(' ' = 2, 'G9' = 2, 'F1' = 2,
                                   'F1A0B' = 2)) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical prognostic stress test')
}
```

A direct check of the covariance matrices explains it (Table
\@ref(tab:tab-pd)). Each strength-0.6 cell on those two pathways, and
$c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$ at $c_{bm} = 0.45$, has a joint matrix that is not
positive definite on all `r V('h_npaths')` Hybrid paths. The repair
replaced it with a nearby matrix before any data were drawn. The
repair shrank the population on-drug minus off-drug slope of the
outcome on the biomarker. That is the quantity the interaction term
estimates. With no prognostic correlation it is `r V('h_c_none')`.
After repair it was `r V('h_c_pb6')` under the placebo-response
pathway and `r V('h_c_tv6')` under the natural-history pathway. The
power loss is the repair removing part of the interaction from the
data. No analysis could recover it. At strength 0.3 the matrix is
positive definite, with a smallest eigenvalue of `r V('h_eig_pb3')`
under the placebo-response pathway.

```{r tab-pd}
if (has_pdc) {
  tpd <- pdc$summary |>
    filter(pathway != 'progtvgrow',
           !(pathway == 'none' & c_bm == 0),
           c_bm == 0.45 | strength == 0.6) |>
    mutate(Pathway = ifelse(pathway == 'none', 'none',
                            path_lab[pathway])) |>
    transmute(Pathway, Strength = sprintf('%.1f', strength),
              `$c_{bm}$` = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
              `Paths repaired` = paths_repaired,
              `Min. eigenvalue` = f3(min_eigenvalue),
              `Contrast, raw` = fs2(contrast_raw),
              `Contrast, repaired` = fs2(contrast_repaired))
  knitr::kable(tpd, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = 'Historical exhibit: positive definiteness of the raw
      joint covariance matrix on the Hybrid paths, and the population
      on-drug minus off-drug slope of the outcome on the biomarker
      before and after the silent repair. Computed from the matrix
      under the simcore2026 SDs, no simulation
      (\\texttt{30-check-prognostic-confound-pd.R}).') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical positive-definiteness check')
}
```

Before the artifact was found, the loss was read as patient-level
variance that a random intercept could not absorb. G9 was refitted
with a random slope on time, on expectancy, and on both, in
`r V('re_ncell')` cells at `r V('re_reps')` replicates. `r V('re_n6')`
of those cells are repaired strength-0.6 cells. The three variants
matched plain G9 to within `r V('re_dmax')` in rejection rate in every
cell (Table \@ref(tab:tab-re)). The largest paired per-replicate
difference was `r V('m12_dmax')`. Non-convergence reached
`r V('re_nonconv')` percent for the variant with both slopes. The DGP
has no patient-specific slope, so there was no variance for a random
slope to absorb. The check shows only that the slopes cost nothing
there.

```{r tab-re}
if (has_re_h) {
  re_lab <- c(G9 = 'G9', G9rs = '+ slope on $w_t$',
              G9re = '+ slope on $\\eta_t$', G9rse = '+ both')
  tre <- re_h |>
    mutate(Cell = sprintf('%s, $c_{bm} = %.2f$, $N = %d$',
                          ifelse(pathway == 'none', 'none',
                                 paste(path_lab[pathway], strength)),
                          c_bm, N),
           Method = re_lab[method]) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tre, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Historical exhibit: rejection rate of G9 and
      its three random-slope variants (simcore2026 parameter set,
      Hybrid, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, %s replicates). The strength-0.6
      rows were simulated under repaired matrices.', V('re_reps'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical random-slope runs')
}
```

The published-set rerun applied the current default, which refuses an
infeasible matrix. Of its `r V('n6_cells')` strength-0.6 cells on the
three correlation pathways, `r V('n6_refused')` were refused and
`r V('n6_ran')` ran. The refused cells are exactly the configurations
that the historical check found infeasible. The cells that ran set
$c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$ with no true interaction, which is feasible. Under
the current code a repaired cell cannot be simulated without an
explicit option.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## What the expectancy terms are for {#sec-expectancy}

The placebo-response amplitude scales with $\eta_t$. In the Hybrid
design $\eta_t$ differs between on-drug and off-drug visits. A
biomarker correlated with the placebo response therefore acquires an
on/off slope difference with no true interaction. Under the
simcore2026 SDs the population contrast was `r V('h_c_pb3n')` at
$c_{bm,PB} = 0.3$ and `r V('h_c_pb6n')` at 0.6, against
`r V('h_c_none')` for the interaction at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ (historical,
Table \@ref(tab:tab-pd)). The placebo-response SD is
`r V('sig_pb_sc')` in the simcore2026 set and `r V('sig_pb')` in the
published set. The contrast scales with that SD. It has not been
recomputed under the published set.

The published-set runs show the consequence. Under the
placebo-response pathway the G-family estimate moved away from zero
with no interaction present (Section \@ref(sec-grid)). The bias was
small against the standard error at $N = 70$ and produced no excess
rejection there. At $N = 280$ it did (Section \@ref(sec-largen)).
The F-family, whose $B^c_i\eta_t$ term absorbs the contrast, stayed
inside the band at every $N$ examined. The earlier conclusion that
the expectancy terms add nothing came from the simcore2026 runs. It
does not hold under the published parameter values.

## The joint recommendation {#sec-recommend}

The two companion papers give one recommendation between them.

- For a biomarker believed to be predictive only, use G10: the
  exposure-weighted indicator with the half-life chosen by AIC on the
  model without the interaction, tested with CR2
  [@pmsimstats-paper02].
- Where the biomarker may also be prognostic, add the
  design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$. This is F1A0,
  or its bootstrap-calibrated form F1A0B. F1A0 and G10 differ only in
  those two terms.
- Where the biomarker may predict the rate of natural-history change,
  also add a biomarker-by-time term. This step is provisional until
  the block of Section \@ref(sec-bmt) is run.

F1, which fixes the half-life at 0.2 week, is not recommended. It
loses power wherever that value is wrong (Section \@ref(sec-gvf)).
Two questions remain for F1A0B. Its bootstrap calibration may be
unnecessary once the selection excludes the interaction. Its cost
against G10 without a prognostic effect is measured here on one grid
only.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

The published-set results come from one parameter set and one
correlation structure ($\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$). Most cells are on
the Hybrid design at $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week. The prognostic correlations
are correlations of a single latent biomarker with the components.
The feasibility bound is a property of that parameterization. The
large-sample cells have no confound-free counterpart at the same $N$.
The trend pathway was simulated at one coefficient, one sample size
and one half-life. Its remedy has not been simulated. The
placebo-response contrast has not been recomputed under the published
SDs. The random-slope variants were fitted only to historical,
partly repaired cells under a DGP without patient-specific slopes.
Comparisons with the block A reference are across jobs and unpaired.
Cells within a job share random-number streams, so counts of cells
inside a band are not independent confirmations.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. A constant prognostic shift is absorbed exactly by the biomarker
   main effect. It cannot move the interaction estimate.
2. Inside the feasibility bounds, the correlation pathways left the G9
   and G10 Type I error inside the band at $N \le 70$.
3. A biomarker correlated with the placebo response biases the
   G-family estimate. Under the published parameter values the bias
   inflated the size of G9 and G10 at $N = 280$. The expectancy terms
   removed it.
4. A biomarker that predicts the natural-history trend biases every
   analysis examined. The expectancy terms absorb part of the bias.
   The biomarker-by-time remedy is pending.
5. The power loss once attributed to a prognostic correlation of 0.6
   was produced by the silent repair of infeasible matrices. Under the
   current default those cells are refused.
6. For a biomarker that may be prognostic, add $\eta_t$ and
   $B^c_i\eta_t$ to G10. The result is F1A0.

# (APPENDIX) Appendix {-}

# Absorption of a constant shift {#sec-absorb}

Let $X$ be the fixed-effects design matrix of any analysis here. It
contains the biomarker main effect $B^c_i$. The constant shift adds
$b_{TV}\sigma_{TV} z_i$ to every outcome of participant $i$. Since
$z_i$ is an affine function of $B^c_i$, the shift vector lies in the
column space of $X$. For fixed variance parameters the generalized
least-squares estimate then changes only in the coefficients of the
intercept and $B^c_i$. The residuals are unchanged. REML and ML
estimates of the variance parameters depend on the data only through
those residuals, so they are unchanged too. AIC selection compares
fits whose likelihoods are unchanged, so it selects the same
half-life. CR2 standard errors depend on the residuals and the design
only. The interaction estimate, its standard error and its $p$-value
are therefore identical, replicate by replicate. The stored data
confirm it (Section \@ref(sec-stress)).
